en: I shall now explain the distinction between the first and third [houses] when conjoined with Vargottama [planets], [using the verse] beginning with "rugṇa," where the letter *ga* occurs everywhere except in the word *parukṇa*. 1.

In the words *gnā*, *agnunā*, *agneṣu*, and also in the word *magna*—whether preceded by the vowel *ā* or the vowel *a*, and even when preceded by *ā*—the third consonant is *r*. In the words *rukme*, *jānu*, and *akna*, the letter *k* [is the third]. In the words *agman*, *prasugma*, *āgman*, *yutayuṅ*, *tigma*, *jagmuḥ*, *gmi*, and *yāsrami*, it is like *g*.

The third letter of the word *śagma* is [the same as] the first syllable here in *śakman*. 3. Everywhere, when followed by the letter *n*, the letter *t* becomes *n*, with the exception of the words *udna* and *mṛdna*; likewise in *admaṃ chinnadmi*, *admi-pradaṃ*, *icdmi-śūtā*, *śakādodma*, *bhinadmi*, and *admnā*. 4.

"vidme," "api," "sadma," "iti," "ca," "dadmahe," "api," "tye," "api"—these words, as well as every *ja* sound joined with a *ka*, likewise [occur] among the best; and in "yāci," "jātana," and "cimī," there is a *ca* for both.
Thus is the definition of the division of the first and third syllables.
